rationale: States the general date of application: 'This Regulation shall apply from 30 December 2024.'
A derogation the need asks for: Titles III and IV apply from 30 June 2024. The corpus has no title headings, so they can only be cited by number.
The second derogation: the listed provisions apply from 29 June 2023. One idea, so no span, although it is the longest node of the corpus.
Entry into force, twenty days after publication, is a different concept from application: useful to avoid confusing them, not an answer.
Transitional regime: providers already operating may continue until 1 July 2026. Related to timing, not the date of application.
Hard negative: its own text is identical, byte for byte, to MiCA Article 149(1), but it is DORA's entry into force.
Hard negative: 'It shall apply from 17 January 2025' is DORA's date of application, a plausible wrong date.
The prohibition for the actor of the need: crypto-asset service providers shall not grant interest when providing services related to e-money tokens.
Turns 'a return for keeping' into interest: any remuneration or benefit related to how long the token is held is treated as interest.
Turns 'euro-pegged stablecoin' into e-money token: a crypto-asset that references the value of one official currency.
The same prohibition for issuers: related, but a different actor.
Definition of crypto-asset service provider; the need already names the actor.
The asset-referenced token definition excludes e-money tokens; it helps rule out the other category.
Hard negative: the parallel prohibition for issuers of asset-referenced tokens, the wrong token category.
Hard negative: the same prohibition for asset-referenced tokens, with the same article title as Article 50; the wrong category.
Hard negative: the definition of interest for asset-referenced tokens, twin of Article 50(3).
The rule that governs the timing: submissions are due within the time limits to be laid down under Article 20, first paragraph, point (a)(ii). It says where the limit comes from, not the number.
Names the initial notification as one of the submissions.
The provision Article 19(4) refers to: the standards shall determine the time limits for the initial notification and each report.
Related qualifier: different time limits may reflect specificities of financial sectors. That sentence sits in the own text of point (a) because of a known parser limitation, hence the span.
The intermediate report, later in the same sequence.
The final report, later in the same sequence.
The general obligation to report major ICT-related incidents to the competent authority.
Definition of major ICT-related incident, which the need presupposes.
Investment firms are within the scope of DORA.
Hard negative: 17 July 2024 is the deadline for the draft standards of the ESAs, not a notification deadline.
Hard negative: 'without undue delay' applies to informing clients, not to the initial notification to the authority.
